title: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon Tops Mercor's APEX-Agents Leaderboard With First Mean Score Above 90%

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Google's Gemini 4 Carbon debuted at No. 1 on Mercor's APEX-Agents leaderboard with an 84.2% Pass@1 score and a 90.4% mean, becoming the only evaluated model to average above 90% across multi-step tasks in investment banking, management consulting and corporate law. Carbon beat second-place Gemini 4 Argon at 82.4% Pass@1 and 87.4% mean and third-place Claude Sonnet 5.5 at 75.5% Pass@1 and 83.7% mean, taking first place in management consulting at 91.9% and investment banking at 86.9% while placing second in corporate law at 73.8%, 2.9 percentage points behind Argon's 76.7%.

Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas also said early evaluations showed Gemini 4 Carbon set a state-of-the-art score on the Wide-And-Deep-Research (WANDR) benchmark and called it the strongest model tested so far for long-form research and answer quality. He said Perplexity will roll out Carbon to all Pro and Max subscribers inside Computer once it has sufficient token capacity. Meanwhile, TestingCatalog reported that Google has been testing a Carbon-H build on Arena under the alias Argon 4 since Oct. 31, while Google engineer Sumit Bagri noted Carbon scored 64.8% on Terminal-Bench-Science and cut cheating attempts on Terminal-Bench 4.0 to 0.4%.

Released two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon, Carbon is currently restricted to vetted cybersecurity defenders in Google's Fairwind Program ahead of wider availability, with launch pricing at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, a 50% discount from standard $4 and $20 rates. Carbon earlier took first place on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index v5 at 59 and Arena's Text Arena at 1,528 points, while placing second behind Claude Opus 5.5 on Coding Agent and Agent Arena leaderboards at 23% to 72% lower cost per task. Vector News reported that independent verification covers only one of Google's three cybersecurity benchmark claims—88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, 54.8% on ExploitGym and 71.0% on CWE-bench—and developer Paradite noted that Carbon's self-reported 65.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 trailed Opus 5.5's 66.4% despite ranking ahead in Artificial Analysis's run.

Exciting news: Gemini 4 Carbon (High) from @GoogleDeepMind  just made a huge debut on Arena, landing #1 in Text Arena, #2 in Agent Arena, and #4 in Code Arena: WebDev. Back at the top, Gemini 4 Carbon delivers frontier intelligence and reshapes the Pareto frontier across three arenas.

In Agent Arena, Gemini 4 Carbon ranks #2 with a +16.2% net improvement across +21.9K real-world agentic sessions from our global community, surpassing top models GPT-6 Astra and Fable-5.1. At $1.80 median cost per task, Gemini 4 Carbon (High) costs 72% less than the #1 ranked Claude Opus 5.5 (Max).

Its standouts by key signals:
- #1 Steerability (+18.6%): can the model course-correct when you push back?
- #2 Praise vs Complaint (+37.9%): implicit sentiment in users' reactions
- #3 Confirmed Success (+18.7%): explicit “yes, that worked” from users

In Code Arena: WebDev, Carbon scored 1768 pts landing #4:
- Just 2 pts below #3 Claude Sonnet 5.5 (xHigh), at 1770 pts
- 89 pts above #11 Gemini 4 Argon (High), at 1679 pts

By category, it ranks #3 in Gaming and Simulations, and #5 in Brand & Marketing.

In Text Arena, Gemini 4 Carbon (High) is the new #1 with 1528 pts, now ahead of Gemini 4 Argon (High) at #2 with 1520 pts.

Congrats to the @GoogleDeepMind team on this huge milestone!

selectedTweets.text:
Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon is the new #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, and second only to Claude Opus 5.5 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index

Gemini 4 Carbon scores 59 on Intelligence Index v5, driven by leading performance in complex reasoning, knowledge, and scientific tasks. It also has large gains in coding and knowledge work, particularly when compared to other Gemini models, but it is not leading in all these areas.

As with launch of Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 4 Carbon is being rolled out to selected users and is not yet publicly available. Google is offering a 50% launch discount, with no confirmed end date. All our charts and figures use standard pricing for both Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon.

Key results for Gemini 4 Carbon with high reasoning:
➤ Gemini 4 Carbon leads the Intelligence Index v5, with the #1 score in 4 of the 9 Index evaluations: HLE-Diamond, Terminal-Bench-Science, AA-Omniscience, AutomationBench-AA. Carbon makes substantial gains elsewhere but is not leading in coding and knowledge work

➤ Behind only Claude Opus 5.5 on coding agents: With Antigravity CLI, Gemini 4 Carbon (high) scores 59 only 3 points behind Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 62) on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index. Carbon ranks second on both Terminal-Bench 4.0 (64%) and FrontierCode v1.1 (51%), behind Claude Opus 5.5 (max) at 56%. Google has historically underperformed in this area and so this improvement stands out

➤ Improved agentic knowledge work, but not yet leading: On AA-Briefcase, Gemini 4 Carbon (high) scores 1609 Elo, a 126-point improvement over Gemini 4 Argon (high, 1483), but still behind models including Grok 4.7 (xhigh, 1638), Muse Wonder (max, 1659) and Kimi K3.1 Pro (1678). The largest gain comes from Presentation, up 293 Elo to 1598, alongside a 120-point improvement in Analytical Quality to 1671

➤ Lower Cost per Task than Claude Opus 5.5 for comparable overall intelligence: Gemini 4 Carbon costs $7.76 per Intelligence Index task, ~23% less than Claude Opus 5.5 (max, $10.04) but ~1.2x GPT-6 Astra (max, $6.25). It uses 123k output tokens per task, 29% fewer than Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 173k). At the same $4/$20 standard pricing, its Cost per Task is in line with Gemini 4 Argon ($7.68), while scoring 9 points higher on the Intelligence Index

➤ Leading AA-Omniscience v1.1 score, with low hallucination: Gemini 4 Carbon scores 54 on our recently updated AA-Omniscience v1.1, 6 points ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 48) and 8 points ahead of Gemini 4 Argon (46). Accuracy (% correct) rises 10 points over Argon to 58%, while its hallucination rate rises from 4% to 11%. This is still the second lowest of any model, behind only Argon, compared with 50% for both Claude Opus 5.5 (max) and GPT-6 Astra (max)

Key model details:
➤ Context Window: 1M tokens
➤ Multimodality: Text, image, video, and speech input, with text output
➤ Pricing: $4/$20 per 1M input/output tokens, the same as Gemini 4 Argon’s standard pricing, with a 50% discount. Cached input tokens receive a 95% discount ($0.20 per 1M)

Congratulations to the @GoogleDeepMind team!
